content:
The Bahrain Grand Prix is being broadcast live for free on Apple TV this weekend, no subscription required. Interestingly, the Bahrain Grand Prix is actually being held at Sepang in Malaysia.

Normally you need a paid subscription to watch F1 on Apple TV, but this weekend everyone can watch for free. You can catch up on the qualifying replay to prepare for tonight's live race - convert Eastern Time 3 AM to Hong Kong time yourself.

Just download the Apple TV app on a supported device, be in the US, and stay up late to watch the live broadcast.

Broadcast coverage begins at 1:50 AM Eastern Time, with the main race scheduled for a 3:00 AM start. Of course, if you want to get to bed earlier, you can always watch the replay afterwards.

The Apple TV app is available on Apple devices, Amazon Fire Stick, Roku, PlayStation, Xbox, Android, and more. You can also watch via browser at tv.apple.com.

Qualifying took place this morning, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen taking the first pole position of the season, Lewis Hamilton second, and championship leader Kim Antonelli third. This is Red Bull's most promising shot at a win so far this year.

You may be wondering why the Bahrain Grand Prix is being held in Malaysia. Normally, the Bahrain round would take place early in the season, but due to the ongoing conflict in Iran, the Bahrain round was cancelled, and the organisers decided to sponsor a race being held elsewhere in the world.

Although Sepang is no longer on the official F1 calendar, the circuit is very popular with fans, and several exciting races are expected to take place there.

Just to reiterate - you can watch for free on the Apple TV app, no subscription required. The main race starts at 3:00 AM Eastern Time, with live coverage beginning at 1:50 AM.
